exam.title: 2014年全国硕士研究生招生考试英语（二）真题

passages.title: Section I: Use of English
passages.content:
Thinner isn't always better. A number of studies have [1] that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight. And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually [2]. For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women. [3], among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an [4] of good health.

Of even greater [5] is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define. It is often defined [6] body mass index, or BMI. BMI [7] body mass divided by the square of height. An adult with a BMI of 18 to 25 is often considered to be normal weight. Between 25 and 30 is overweight. And over 30 is considered obese. Obesity, [8], can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese.

While such numerical standards seem [9], they are not. Obesity is probably less a matter of weight than body fat. Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, [10] others with a low BMI may be in poor [11]. For example, many collegiate and professional football players [12] as obese, though their percentage body fat is low. Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a [13] BMI.

Today we have a(n) [14] to label obesity as a disgrace. The overweight are sometimes [15] in the media with their faces covered. Stereotypes [16] with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success. Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese. [17] very young children tend to look down on the overweight, and teasing about body build has long been a problem in schools.

Negative attitudes toward obesity, [18] in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity [19]. My own hospital system has banned sugary drinks from its facilities. Many employers have instituted weight loss and fitness initiatives. Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign [20] childhood obesity, even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
What would you do with $590m? This is now a question for Gloria MacKenzie, an 84-year-old widow who recently emerged from her small, tin-roofed house in Florida to collect the biggest undivided lottery jackpot in history. If she hopes her new-found fortune will yield lasting feelings of fulfilment, she could do worse than read Happy Money by Elizabeth Dunn and Michael Norton.

These two academics use an array of behavioral research to show that the most rewarding ways to spend money can be counterintuitive. Fantasies of great wealth often involve visions of fancy cars and extravagant homes. Yet satisfaction with these material purchases wears off fairly quickly. What was once exciting and new becomes old-hat; regret creeps in. It is far better to spend money on experiences, say Ms Dunn and Mr Norton, like interesting trips, unique meals or even going to the cinema. These purchases often become more valuable with time — as stories or memories — particularly if they involve feeling more connected to others.

This slim volume is packed with tips to help wage slaves as well as lottery winners get the most "happiness bang for your buck." It seems most people would be better off if they could shorten their commutes to work, spend more time with friends and family and less of it watching television (something the average American spends a whopping two months a year doing, and is hardly jollier for it). Buying gifts or giving to charity is often more pleasurable than purchasing things for oneself, and luxuries are most enjoyable when they are consumed sparingly. This is apparently the reason McDonald's restricts the availability of its popular McRib — a marketing trick that has turned the pork sandwich into an object of obsession.

Readers of Happy Money are clearly a privileged lot, anxious about fulfilment, not hunger. Money may not quite buy happiness, but people in wealthier countries are generally happier than those in poor ones. Yet the link between feeling good and spending money on others can be seen among rich and poor people around the world, and scarcity enhances the pleasure of most things for most people. Not everyone will agree with the authors' policy ideas, which range from mandating more holiday time to reducing tax incentives for American homebuyers. But most people will come away from this book believing it was money well spent.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
An article in Scientific American has pointed out that empirical research says that, actually, you think you're more beautiful than you are. We have a deep-seated need to feel good about ourselves and we naturally employ a number of self-enhancing strategies to achieve this. Social psychologists have amassed oceans of research into what they call the "above average effect", or "illusory superiority", and shown that, for example, 70% of us rate ourselves as above average in leadership, 93% in driving and 85% at getting on well with others — all obviously statistical impossibilities.

We rose-tint our memories and put ourselves into self-affirming situations. We become defensive when criticised, and apply negative stereotypes to others to boost our own esteem. We stalk around thinking we're hot stuff.

Psychologist and behavioural scientist Nicholas Epley oversaw a key study into self-enhancement and attractiveness. Rather than have people simply rate their beauty compared with others, he asked them to identify an original photograph of themselves from a lineup including versions that had been altered to appear more and less attractive. Visual recognition, reads the study, is "an automatic psychological process, occurring rapidly and intuitively with little or no apparent conscious deliberation". If the subjects quickly chose a falsely flattering image — which most did — they genuinely believed it was really how they looked.

Epley found no significant gender difference in responses. Nor was there any evidence that those who self-enhanced the most (that is, the participants who thought the most positively doctored pictures were real) were doing so to make up for profound insecurities. In fact, those who thought that the images higher up the attractiveness scale were real directly corresponded with those who showed other markers for having higher self-esteem. "I don't think the findings that we have are any evidence of personal delusion," says Epley. "It's a reflection simply of people generally thinking well of themselves." If you are depressed, you won't be self-enhancing.

Knowing the results of Epley's study, it makes sense that many people hate photographs of themselves viscerally — on one level, they don't even recognise the person in the picture as themselves. Facebook, therefore, is a self-enhancer's paradise, where people can share only the most flattering photos, the cream of their wit, style, beauty, intellect and lifestyles. It's not that people's profiles are dishonest, says Catalina Toma of Wisconsin-Madison University, "but they portray an idealised version of themselves."

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
The concept of man versus machine is at least as old as the industrial revolution, but this phenomenon tends to be most acutely felt during economic downturns and fragile recoveries. And yet, it would be a mistake to think we are right now simply experiencing the painful side of a boom and bust cycle. Certain jobs have gone away for good, outmoded by machines. Since technology has such an insatiable appetite for eating up human jobs, this phenomenon will continue to restructure our economy in ways we cannot immediately foresee.

When there is rapid improvement in the price and performance of technology, jobs that were once thought to be immune from automation suddenly become threatened. This argument has attracted a lot of attention, via the success of the book Race Against the Machine, by Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee, who both hail from MIT's Center for Digital Business.

This is a powerful argument, and a scary one. And yet, John Hagel, author of The Power of Pull and other books, says Brynjolfsson and McAfee miss the reason why these jobs are so vulnerable to technology in the first place.

Hagel says we have designed jobs in the U.S. that tend to be "tightly scripted" and "highly standardized" ones that leave no room for "individual initiative or creativity." In short, these are the types of jobs that machines can perform much better at than human beings. That is how we have put a giant target sign on the backs of American workers, Hagel says.

It's time to reinvent the formula for how work is conducted, since we are still relying on a very 20th century notion of work, Hagel says. In our rapidly changing economy, we more than ever need people in the workplace who can take initiative and exercise their imagination "to respond to unexpected events". That is not something machines are good at. They are designed to perform very predictable activities.

As Hagel notes, Brynjolfsson and McAfee indeed touched on this point in their book. We need to reframe race against the machine as race with the machine. In other words, we need to look at the ways in which machines can augment human labor rather than replace it. So then the problem is not really about technology, but rather, "how do we innovate our institutions and our work practices?"

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
When the government talks about infrastructure contributing to the economy the focus is usually on roads, railways, broadband and energy. Housing is seldom mentioned.

Why is that? To some extent the housing sector must shoulder the blame. We have not been good at communicating the real value that housing can contribute to economic growth. Then there is the scale of the typical housing project. It is hard to shove for attention among multibillion-pound infrastructure projects, so it is inevitable that the attention is focused elsewhere. But perhaps the most significant reason is that the issue has always been so politically charged.

Nevertheless, the affordable housing situation is desperate. Waiting lists increase all the time and we are simply not building enough new homes.

The comprehensive spending review offers an opportunity for the government to help rectify this. It needs to put historical prejudices to one side and take some steps to address our urgent housing need.

There are some indications that it is preparing to do just that. The communities minister, Don Foster, has hinted that George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, may introduce more flexibility to the current cap on the amount that local authorities can borrow against their housing stock debt. Evidence shows that 60,000 extra new homes could be built over the next five years if the cap were lifted, increasing GDP by 0.6%.

Ministers should also look at creating greater certainty in the rental environment, which would have a significant impact on the ability of registered providers to fund new developments from revenues.

But it is not just down to the government. While these measures would be welcome in the short term, we must face up to the fact that the existing £4.5bn programme of grants to fund new affordable housing, set to expire in 2015, is unlikely to be extended beyond then. The Labour party has recently announced that it will retain a large part of the coalition's spending plans if it returns to power. The housing sector needs to accept that we are very unlikely to ever return to the era of large-scale public grants. We need to adjust to this changing climate.

While the government's commitment to long-term funding may have changed, the very pressing need for more affordable housing is real and is not going away.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Emerging in the late Sixties and reaching a peak in the Seventies, Land Art was one of a range of new forms, including Body Art, Performance Art, Action Art and Installation Art, which pushed art beyond the traditional confines of the studio and gallery. Rather than portraying landscape, land artists used the physical substance of the land itself as their medium.

The British land art, typified by Richard Long's piece, was not only more domestically scaled, but a lot quirkier than its American counterpart. Indeed, while you might assume that an exhibition of Land Art would consist only of records of works rather than the works themselves, Long's photograph of his work is the work. Since his "action" is in the past, the photograph is its sole embodiment.

That might seem rather an obscure point, but it sets the tone for an exhibition that contains a lot of black-and-white photographs and relatively few natural objects.

Long is Britain's best-known Land Artist and his Stone Circle, a perfect ring of purplish rocks from Portishead beach laid out on the gallery floor, represents the elegant, rarefied side of the form. The Boyle Family, on the other hand, stand for its dirty, urban aspect. Comprising artists Mark Boyle and Joan Hills and their children, they recreated random sections of the British landscape on gallery walls. Their Olaf Street Study, a square of brick-strewn waste ground, is one of the few works here to embrace the commonplaceness that characterises most of our experience of the landscape most of the time.

Parks feature, particularly in the earlier works, such as John Hilliard's very funny Across the Park, in which a long-haired stroller is variously smiled at by a pretty girl and unwittingly assaulted in a sequence of images that turn out to be different parts of the same photograph.

Generally however British land artists preferred to get away from towns, gravitating towards landscapes that are traditionally considered beautiful such as the Lake District or the Wiltshire Downs. While it probably wasn't apparent at the time, much of this work is permeated by a spirit of romantic escapism that the likes of Wordsworth would have readily understood. Derek Jarman's yellow-tinted film Towards Avebury, a collection of long, mostly still shots of the Wiltshire landscape, evokes a tradition of English landscape painting stretching from Samuel Palmer to Paul Nash.

In the case of Hamish Fulton, you can't help feeling that the Scottish artist has simply found a way of making his love of walking pay. A typical work, such as Seven Days, consists of a single beautiful black-and-white photograph taken on an epic walk, with the mileage and number of days taken listed beneath. British Land Art as shown in this well selected, but relatively modestly scaled exhibition wasn't about imposing on the landscape, more a kind of landscape-orientated light conceptual art created passing through. It had its origins in the great outdoors, but the results were as gallery-bound as the paintings of Turner and Constable.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第一段第二句：A number of studies have [1] that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight。
【命题解密】考查动词语义辨析。首句指出“更瘦并不总是更健康”，第二句用科学研究结果加以印证：多项研究已得出结论（concluded），正常体重者实际上比超重者更容易患上某些疾病，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A] denied（否认）与顺承论证逻辑相悖；[C] doubted（怀疑）表否定态度，不合文意；[D] ensured（确保）通常不用于确保患病等负面结果的发生。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第一段第三句：And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually [2]。
【命题解密】考查形容词词义辨析。本句与上句构成顺承关系，且下句举出较重女性更不易缺钙为例，说明在某些健康状况下超重其实起到保护性作用（protective），故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B] dangerous（危险的）与下文不易缺钙的正向例证相反；[C] sufficient（足够的）与健康状况搭配不当且不符合上下文语义；[D] troublesome（麻烦的）带有负面色彩，与文意相悖。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第一段第五句句首：[3], among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an indicator of good health。
【命题解密】考查逻辑副词辨析。前一句说明女性群体中体重较重的益处，本句紧接着指出老年人群体中稍微超重也对健康有益。两者属于并列类比关系，[C] Likewise（同样地）准确衔接前后两组相似例证，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A] Instead（相反）与[B] However（然而）均表转折对立，与并行例证不符；[D] Therefore（因此）表因果关系，女性与老年人的情况并无因果联系。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第一段第五句：...among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an [4] of good health。
【命题解密】考查名词辨析。本句旨在说明老年人稍微超重往往是身体健康的标志与表征。indicator意为“指示物，标志”，an indicator of good health准确传达出“健康良好的标志”，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B] objective（目标）指“超重是健康的目标”，不合逻辑；[C] origin（起源）夸大了体重对健康的决定性；[D] example（例子）中超重不能作为“身体健康”的同类实例。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段首句：Of even greater [5] is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define。
【命题解密】考查名词辨析与倒装结构。本句采用“of+抽象名词”作表语的倒装结构，指出“肥胖其实很难定义”这一事实甚至更令人担忧、更值得关注。of concern为固定搭配，意为“令人关切的、重要的”，故选[D]。
【错项排除】[A] impact（影响）、[B] relevance（相关性/意义）与[C] assistance（帮助）均不如of even greater concern贴合下文对BMI标准误区的批判重心。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段第二句：It is often defined [6] body mass index, or BMI。
【命题解密】考查介词短语辨析。此处说明肥胖在常规医学中往往是“根据/依照”身体质量指数（BMI）来界定的。in terms of意为“依据、从……角度/标准而言”，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B] in case of（万一，以防）；[C] in favor of（支持，赞成）；[D] in respects of并非地道英语搭配（常用in respect of），均与通过BMI标准进行定义无关。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段第三句：BMI [7] body mass divided by the square of height。
【命题解密】考查动词词义辨析。本句给出BMI指数的计算公式，即“BMI等于体重除以身高的平方”。equals意为“（数值、大小等）等于”，符合数学定义表达，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A] measures（测量）的宾语通常为长度、尺寸等物理量而非除法公式；[B] determines（决定）将公式与指标的因果关系颠倒；[D] modifies（修改）意为人为调整，不合公式运算语义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段末句：Obesity, [8], can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese。
【命题解密】考查插入语逻辑辨析。前文按BMI数值划分出正常、超重与肥胖三大类别，此处进一步说明“肥胖”这一类别又可依次划分为中度、重度和极重度三个亚类。in turn意为“进而、反过来、转而”，体现层层递进的分类关系，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A] in essence（本质上）与分类列举无关；[B] in contrast（相比之下）错加对比关系；[D] in part（部分地）与全面划分为三类逻辑不符。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段首句：While such numerical standards seem [9], they are not。
【命题解密】考查形容词辨析。上段列举了一系列清晰的BMI划分数值，本段首句借助While引导让步转折，指出这些数字标准“表面上看起来直接明了（straightforward），实则并非如此”，从而引出BMI测量的局限性，故选[D]。
【错项排除】[A] complicated（复杂的）与下句“they are not”转折后的“肥胖难以界定”产生逻辑冲突；[B] conservative（保守的）；[C] variable（多变的）均非BMI固定区间数值给人的直观印象。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段第三句：Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, [10] others with a low BMI may be in poor [11]。
【命题解密】考查并列连词语义逻辑。前半句说高BMI的人其实可能非常健壮，后半句说低BMI的人反而可能健康不佳。前后形成鲜明对比，while作并列连词可意为“然而、而”，精准衔接对比两分句，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A] so（因此）和[C] since（因为）均错置因果逻辑；[D] unless（除非）误设条件关系。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段第三句后半句：...others with a low BMI may be in poor [11]。
【命题解密】考查名词固定搭配。与前半句extremely fit（极其健壮）形成对照，此处表示BMI较低的人体格或健康状况可能很差。in poor shape意为“身体状况不佳、状态差”，为常见固定搭配，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B] spirit（情绪/精神，in poor spirit指士气低落）偏离身体健康话题；[C] balance（平衡）和[D] taste（品味）均不与in poor搭配表示体质好坏。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段第四句：For example, many collegiate and professional football players [12] as obese, though their percentage body fat is low。
【命题解密】考查动词固定搭配。全句以体脂率极低的橄榄球运动员为例，说明他们在BMI标准下竟“算作/被归类为”肥胖人群。qualify as意为“符合标准、可算作是”，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A] start as（最初作为）、[C] retire as（退休时担任）、[D] stay as（保持作为）均无法表达按数值标准被界定归类的含义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段末句：Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a [13] BMI。
【命题解密】考查形容词上下文对比。Conversely承接上文“高BMI却体脂低”的运动员案例，给出相反情形：骨架较小的人可能体脂率偏高，却拥有一个看似“正常的（normal）”BMI指数，从而再次证明BMI失准，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A] strange（奇怪的）；[B] changeable（易变的）；[D] constant（恒定的）均无法与上文形成“体脂高 vs BMI正常”的鲜明反差。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段首句：Today we have a(n) [14] to label obesity as a disgrace。
【命题解密】考查名词辨析与习惯搭配。下文提到媒体遮挡肥胖者面部、将肥胖与懒惰挂钩以及校园欺凌，可见当代社会普遍存在一种把肥胖视作耻辱的倾向。have a tendency to do sth意为“有做某事的倾向”，故选[D]。
【错项排除】[A] option（选择，与a(n)搭配多指具体可选项）；[B] reason（理由）和[C] opportunity（机会）代入后意为“有理由/有机会羞辱肥胖者”，与作者批判社会偏见的立场不符。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段第二句：The overweight are sometimes [15] in the media with their faces covered。
【命题解密】考查动词语义与语境搭配。句中in the media与with their faces covered明确提示新闻媒体报道中的视觉画面处理——超重者在媒体影像中“被拍摄/被呈现（pictured）”时脸部常被遮挡，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A] employed（雇佣）；[C] imitated（模仿）；[D] monitored（监控）均与媒体配图遮面报道不符。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [16] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段第三句：Stereotypes [16] with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success。
【命题解密】考查动词分词短语搭配。句中列举的懒惰、缺乏意志力都是社会加诸于肥胖身上的固有偏见。associated with意为“与……相关联的”，Stereotypes associated with obesity意为“与肥胖相关的刻板印象”，故选[D]。
【错项排除】[A] compared with（与……相比）、[B] combined with（与……结合）、[C] settled with（与……和解）均不与stereotypes搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [17] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段第五句句首：[17] very young children tend to look down on the overweight...
【命题解密】考查上下文递进逻辑。前文提到成年人及教师、雇主、医护人员都对肥胖存有偏见，紧接着本句指出“甚至（Even）”连年幼的孩童也往往看不起超重者。Even在此表强烈递进与惊讶语气，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B] Still（仍然）与[C] Yet（然而）多表转折让步；[D] Only（仅仅）说只有小孩歧视肥胖者，与前文教师、雇主等歧视矛盾。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [18] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第五段首句：Negative attitudes toward obesity, [18] in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity [19]。
【命题解密】考查动词固定搭配。对肥胖的负面态度“立足于/源于（grounded in）”健康顾虑，从而催生了诸多抗击肥胖的政策举措。be grounded in意为“建立在……基础上，基于”，过去分词短语作后置定语，故选[D]。
【错项排除】[A] despised（鄙视）、[B] corrected（纠正）、[C] ignored（忽视）均无法与in health concerns构成合乎逻辑的原因状语定语。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第五段首句末：...have stimulated a number of anti-obesity [19]。
【命题解密】考查名词辨析与下文例证对应。紧随其后的句子列举了三项落地措施：医院禁止含糖饮料、雇主推出健身计划、米歇尔·奥巴马发起全国倡议。能够涵盖这些具体行政和机构举措的词是policies（政策，办法），故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A] discussions（讨论）侧重口头层面；[B] businesses（商业业务）；[D] studies（研究）均无法概括禁售饮料和企业健身体制等行动举措。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第五段末句：Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign [20] childhood obesity...
【命题解密】考查介词词义与语境搭配。米歇尔·奥巴马发起了一场高调的宣传运动，旨在“对抗/遏制”儿童肥胖问题。a campaign against sth意为“针对/反对……的运动”，完全契合下文将其视为国家安全威胁的打击立场，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A] for（支持，赞成）与遏制儿童肥胖的立场相反；[C] with和[D] without均不与campaign搭配表示“对抗某种问题”。

questions.stem: According to Dunn and Norton, which of the following is the most rewarding purchase?
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段第四至五句：“It is far better to spend money on experiences, say Ms Dunn and Mr Norton, like interesting trips, unique meals or even going to the cinema.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。邓恩与诺顿明确建议与其购买汽车豪宅，不如把钱花在难忘的经历上，比如有趣的旅行（interesting trips）或独特的餐食。[B]项“A special tour（一次特别的旅行）”精准同义替换interesting trips，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A] A big house与[C] A stylish car属于上句明确批判满意度会快速消退的物质消费（fancy cars and extravagant homes）；[D] A rich meal偷换了unique meals（独特的餐饮体验），rich强调油腻丰盛/昂贵而非独特记忆。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward Americans' watching TV is
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段第二句：“It seems most people would be better off if they could shorten their commutes to work, spend more time with friends and family and less of it watching television (something the average American spends a whopping two months a year doing, and is hardly jollier for it).”
【命题解密】考查观点态度。作者用a whopping（惊人的、高达）形容美国人每年耗在看电视上的时间长达两个月，并指出他们却并未因此更快乐（hardly jollier for it），建议少看电视以增加幸福感。字里行间体现作者对沉迷看电视的明确批评态度，故选[A] critical。
【错项排除】[B] supportive（支持的）完全相反；[C] sympathetic（同情的）误解了hardly jollier的批评语气；[D] ambiguous（模棱两可的）忽略了作者明确的建议倾向。

questions.stem: McRib is mentioned in Paragraph 3 to show that
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段第三至四句：“...and luxuries are most enjoyable when they are consumed sparingly. This is apparently the reason McDonald's restricts the availability of its popular McRib — a marketing trick that has turned the pork sandwich into an object of obsession.”
【命题解密】考查例证题。麦当劳刻意限制烤汁猪排堡供应期的案例紧承上句论点“适度节制消费奢侈品时才最令人愉悦”，旨在论证“稀缺性通常能增强愉悦体验”，故选[D] rarity generally increases pleasure。
【错项排除】[A]项“消费者不理智”曲解顾客的痴迷；[B]项“流行源于品质”原文未谈及产品品质；[C]项“营销技巧常有效”过度泛化，且McRib案例重在揭示“限量稀缺提升快感”这一心理规律而非赞颂营销。

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, Happy Money

options.text: has left much room for readers' criticism
options.content: has left much room for readers' criticism

options.text: may prove to be a worthwhile purchase
options.content: may prove to be a worthwhile purchase

options.text: has predicted a wider income gap in the US
options.content: has predicted a wider income gap in the US

options.text: may give its readers a sense of achievement
options.content: may give its readers a sense of achievement

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段末两句：“Not everyone will agree with the authors' policy ideas... But most people will come away from this book believing it was money well spent.”
【命题解密】考查推理细节。末句借助But强烈转折指出，尽管并非人人都会赞同书中具体的政策建议，但绝大多数读者读完《快乐金钱》后都会认为“这钱花得很值”（money well spent），故选[B] may prove to be a worthwhile purchase。
【错项排除】[A]项“为读者批评留下很大空间”将Not everyone will agree夸大；[C]项“预测美国收入差距扩大”无中生有，前文只对比了富国与穷国；[D]项“给读者带来成就感”张冠李戴了读者对书中如何花钱获得满足感的认知。

questions.stem: This text mainly discusses how to

options.text: balance feeling good and spending money
options.content: balance feeling good and spending money

options.text: spend large sums of money won in lotteries
options.content: spend large sums of money won in lotteries

options.text: obtain lasting satisfaction from money spent
options.content: obtain lasting satisfaction from money spent

options.text: become more reasonable in spending on luxuries
options.content: become more reasonable in spending on luxuries

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】通读全文主旨，首段引出中奖能否带来“lasting feelings of fulfilment（持久的满足感）”，第二至四段介绍两位学者提出的科学花钱方法并高度评价该书值得买。
【命题解密】考查主旨大意。全文自始至终探讨的核心议题是如何更明智地花钱以获得长期的幸福与满足感，故选[C] obtain lasting satisfaction from money spent。
【错项排除】[A]项“平衡快乐感与花钱”曲解末段“快乐感与替别人花钱的关联”；[B]项“如何花掉彩票巨奖”仅是首段引子；[D]项“更理性购买奢侈品”属于第三段细节之一，无法概括全篇。

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, social psychologists have found that

options.text: illusory superiority is a baseless effect
options.content: illusory superiority is a baseless effect

options.text: our need for leadership is unnatural
options.content: our need for leadership is unnatural

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第一段第三句：“Social psychologists have amassed oceans of research into what they call the 'above average effect', or 'illusory superiority', and shown that, for example, 70% of us rate ourselves as above average in leadership, 93% in driving and 85% at getting on well with others — all obviously statistical impossibilities.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。高达70%、93%和85%的人自认为高于平均水平，这在统计学上是不可能的，证明人们普遍存在“虚幻的优越感”，自我评价高得脱离实际，故选[A] our self-ratings are unrealistically high。
【错项排除】[B]项将“统计上不可能”歪曲为该心理学效应没有根据（baseless）；[C]项将70%自认为领导力超常曲解为对领导力的需求不正常；[D]项“自我美化策略无效”与文中人们借此维持自信的事实相悖。

questions.stem: Visual recognition is believed to be people's
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第三段第二句：“Visual recognition, reads the study, is 'an automatic psychological process, occurring rapidly and intuitively with little or no apparent conscious deliberation'.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。研究报告明文定义“视觉识别”是一种快速、凭借直觉、几乎没有有意识思考的自发心理过程。intuitive response（直觉反应）精准对应intuitively，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A]项rapid matching将心理反应偷换为机械配对；[B]项conscious choice与little or no apparent conscious deliberation彻底相反；[D]项automatic self-defence拼凑了automatic与第二段对批评作防卫反应（defensive）。

questions.stem: Epley found that people with higher self-esteem tended to
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段第二至三句：“In fact, those who thought that the images higher up the attractiveness scale were real directly corresponded with those who showed other markers for having higher self-esteem.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。Epley的实验结果显示，越是将被显著美化的照片当作真实自我的人，其自尊水平（higher self-esteem）的其他测量指标也越高，即自尊心较强的人往往深信自己极具魅力，故选[B] believe in their attractiveness。
【错项排除】[A]项与原文否定“并非为了弥补不安全感（make up for profound insecurities）”相悖；[C]项曲解末句“抑郁的人不会自我美化”；[D]项将“不是个人妄想”篡改为过度简化幻觉。

questions.stem: The word "viscerally" (Line 2, Para. 5) is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第五段第一句：“Knowing the results of Epley's study, it makes sense that many people hate photographs of themselves viscerally — on one level, they don't even recognise the person in the picture as themselves.”
【命题解密】考查词义推断。前文指出视觉识图是瞬间自发且靠直觉的无意识心理过程，所以当人们看到未经美化的真实照片时，由于不认识那个不如想象中漂亮的人，会由衷、本能地排斥讨厌自己的照片。viscerally意为“发自内心/本能地”，与[A] instinctively完全同义，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B] occasionally（偶尔）；[C] particularly（尤其）；[D] aggressively（攻击性地/极力地）均不能与前文的无意识直觉反应呼应。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that Facebook is a self-enhancer's paradise because people can
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第五段第二至三句：“Facebook, therefore, is a self-enhancer's paradise, where people can share only the most flattering photos, the cream of their wit, style, beauty, intellect and lifestyles. It's not that people's profiles are dishonest... 'but they portray an idealised version of themselves.'”
【命题解密】考查细节推断。在Facebook上，人们可以只分享最奉承美化的照片以及机智、品位和生活方式中最精彩的部分，亦即可以筛选隐藏自己平庸、不讨喜的一面，从而构建理想化的个人形象，故选[D] withhold their unflattering sides。
【错项排除】[A]项与下句明文否定“It's not that people's profiles are dishonest”直接矛盾；[B]项“定义传统生活方式”无中生有；[C]项把才智精华偷换为学术/知识追求且以偏概全。

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, economic downturns would

options.text: ease the competition of man vs. machine
options.content: ease the competition of man vs. machine

options.text: highlight machines' threat to human jobs
options.content: highlight machines' threat to human jobs

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第一段第一句：“The concept of man versus machine is at least as old as the industrial revolution, but this phenomenon tends to be most acutely felt during economic downturns and fragile recoveries.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。人机竞争虽历史悠久，但在经济下行与脆弱复苏期间这种感受最为剧烈尖锐，也就是说经济衰退会凸显机器取代人类工作的紧迫威胁，故选[B] highlight machines' threat to human jobs。
【错项排除】[A] ease（缓和）与most acutely felt相反；[C]项颠倒因果，是既有技术加剧失业而非衰退引发技术革命；[D]项将“被机器淘汰的岗位”与“重塑经济结构”混为一谈。

questions.stem: The authors of Race Against the Machine argue that

options.text: technology is diminishing man's job opportunities
options.content: technology is diminishing man's job opportunities

options.text: certain jobs will remain intact after automation
options.content: certain jobs will remain intact after automation

options.text: man will finally win the race against machine
options.content: man will finally win the race against machine

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段第一至二句：“When there is rapid improvement in the price and performance of technology, jobs that were once thought to be immune from automation suddenly become threatened. This argument has attracted a lot of attention, via the success of the book Race Against the Machine...”
【命题解密】考查人物观点。《与机器赛跑》的两位作者主张：随着技术价格下降和性能飞跃，连过去认为不受自动化影响的工作也突然岌岌可危，即技术正在不断蚕食减少人类的就业机会，故选[A] technology is diminishing man's job opportunities。
【错项排除】[B]项颠倒了技术提升与自动化的关系；[C]项与“曾被认为不受影响的工作也受到威胁”相反；[D]项错将书名Race Against the Machine理解为人会赢得竞赛，而书作者重在警示就业缩水。

questions.stem: Hagel argues that jobs in the U.S. are often
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段第一至二句：“Hagel says we have designed jobs in the U.S. that tend to be 'tightly scripted' and 'highly standardized' ones that leave no room for 'individual initiative or creativity'.”
【命题解密】考查人物观点。Hagel一针见血地指出美国工作岗位被设计得高度脚本化、高度标准化，完全没有留给个人主动性与创造力的空间，故选[D] designed against human creativity。
【错项排除】[A]项与不留创造力空间相反；[B]项将scripted与individual杂糅，曲解了限制个性的严格脚本；[C]项把a giant target sign（令工人变成被机器替代的大靶子）偷换为工作缺乏清晰目标。

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, Brynjolfsson and McAfee discussed

options.text: the predictability of machine behavior in practice
options.content: the predictability of machine behavior in practice

options.text: the formula for how work is conducted efficiently
options.content: the formula for how work is conducted efficiently

options.text: the ways machines replace human labor in modern times
options.content: the ways machines replace human labor in modern times

options.text: the necessity of human involvement in the workplace
options.content: the necessity of human involvement in the workplace

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第六段（末段）第一至三句：“As Hagel notes, Brynjolfsson and McAfee indeed touched on this point in their book. We need to reframe race against the machine as race with the machine. In other words, we need to look at the ways in which machines can augment human labor rather than replace it.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。末段首句“this point”虽承接前文，但随后两句直接阐述两位作者书中触及的观点：我们需要寻找机器“增强”而非替代人类劳动的方法，将人与机器的对抗重塑为人机协作，肯定了工作场所中人类参与的不可替代性，故选[D] the necessity of human involvement in the workplace。
【错项排除】[A]与[B]项属于第五段Hagel本人论述内容，并非末段Brynjolfsson与McAfee书中观点；[C]项与原文“增强人类劳动而不是替代它（rather than replace it）”完全相反。

questions.stem: Which of the following could be the most appropriate title for the text?

options.text: How to Innovate Our Work Practices?
options.content: How to Innovate Our Work Practices?

options.text: Can We Win the Race Against Machines?
options.content: Can We Win the Race Against Machines?

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】综合全文脉络，第一、二段提出机器在衰退期吞噬就业岗位引出《与机器赛跑》的焦虑，第三至五段借Hagel指出问题根源在于僵化的工作设计而非技术本身，末段点明应当重塑工作制度与模式、与机器共舞。
【命题解密】考查文章标题。全文围绕“人类能否在这场与机器的角逐中胜出”这一核心悬念层层剥茧并给出制度创新之道，故选[C] Can We Win the Race Against Machines?。
【错项排除】[A]项仅指末段一句总结，无法涵盖前五段背景探讨；[B]项“机器将取代人类”只代表第二段担忧，违背末段人机协作主旨；[D]项偏离全文人机就业主题。

questions.stem: The author believes that the housing sector

options.text: has lost its real value in economy
options.content: has lost its real value in economy

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第二段末句：“But perhaps the most significant reason is that the issue has always been so politically charged.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。在探讨政府谈论基础设施时为何很少提及住房行业的原因时，作者最后强调最关键的症结在于该议题向来具有极强的政治敏感性（politically charged），即住房行业牵涉某些政治因素，故选[D] involves certain political factors。
【错项排除】[A]项与首段seldom mentioned及第二段hard to shove for attention相反；[B]项曲解第二段第二句“未能有效传达自身对经济增长的真实价值”，不等于失去价值；[C]项将to some extent... must shoulder the blame（在某种程度上应负一定责任）过度引申为承担太多责任。

questions.stem: It can be learned that affordable housing has
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第四段第一至二句：“The comprehensive spending review offers an opportunity for the government to help rectify this. It needs to put historical prejudices to one side and take some steps to address our urgent housing need.”
【命题解密】考查细节推断。作者呼吁政府利用综合开支审查的契机“把历史偏见（historical prejudices）放到一边”来纠正住房紧缺局面，由此可推知经济适用房长期以来遭受了政府的偏见，故选[A] suffered government biases。
【错项排除】[B]项与第三段not building enough new homes相悖；[C]项把“综合开支审查提供契机”误套在经济适用房上；[D]项错将民众对严峻房市的绝望（desperate）当作令政府失望。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 5, George Osborne may

options.text: prepare to reduce housing stock debt
options.content: prepare to reduce housing stock debt

options.text: release a lifted GDP growth forecast
options.content: release a lifted GDP growth forecast

options.text: allow greater government debt for housing
options.content: allow greater government debt for housing

options.text: stop local authorities from building homes
options.content: stop local authorities from building homes

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第五段第二至三句：“The communities minister, Don Foster, has hinted that George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, may introduce more flexibility to the current cap on the amount that local authorities can borrow against their housing stock debt.”
【命题解密】考查事实细节。财政大臣George Osborne可能会对地方政府以住房存量债务为抵押的借款上限采取更大的灵活性（即放宽借贷上限），从而允许为住房建设举借更多政府债务，故选[C] allow greater government debt for housing。
【错项排除】[A]项把“提高地方政府举债上限”曲解为“减少住房存量债务”；[B]项把raising GDP by 0.6%的预测数据安在Osborne身上且偷换了前提；[D]项与抬高上限以建6万套新房（build extra new homes）截然相反。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that a stable rental environment would

options.text: lower the costs of registered providers
options.content: lower the costs of registered providers

options.text: lessen the impact of government interference
options.content: lessen the impact of government interference

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第六段：“Ministers should also look at creating greater certainty in the rental environment, which would have a significant impact on the ability of registered providers to fund new developments from revenues.”
【命题解密】考查细节推断。若政府能为租房市场创造更大的确定性与稳定性，将对注册住房供应机构依靠营业收入为新建项目筹集资金（fund new developments）产生显著积极影响，故选[C] contribute to funding new developments。

【命题解密】考查多项对应。德里克·贾曼的黄色调影像作品《前往埃夫伯里》（Towards Avebury）捕捉威尔特郡风光，唤起了从塞缪尔·帕尔默延续至保罗·纳什的英国风景画传统（evokes a tradition of English landscape painting）。选项[C]“reminds people of the English landscape painting tradition”准确对应，故选[C]。

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】定位至第七段第一至二句：“In the case of Hamish Fulton, you can't help feeling that the Scottish artist has simply found a way of making his love of walking pay. A typical work, such as Seven Days, consists of a single beautiful black-and-white photograph taken on an epic walk, with the mileage and number of days taken listed beneath.”
【命题解密】考查多项对应。苏格兰艺术家哈米什·富尔顿把对徒步的热爱融入创作，其代表作《七天》（Seven Days）正是将一次长途史诗般徒步中拍摄的黑白摄影配以里程与天数记录而成。选项[A]“originates from a long walk that the artist took”契合an epic walk，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B]项“说明以风景为导向的轻概念艺术”出自末句，评价的是整场英国大地艺术展的总体特质，而非《七天》单件作品，属于以偏概全干扰。
